slot.brief: A limit at a point where the expression involves |x| or a greatest-integer/greatest-modulus piece; evaluate left and right limits separately and match, or conclude the limit does not exist.

verdicts.working: For x<2, |x−2|=−(x−2), so f(x)=x+1 and the left limit is 3. For x>2, |x−2|=x−2, so f(x)=x+3 and the right limit is 5.

working:
$\dfrac{x^2-4}{x-2}=x+2\to4$; $\dfrac{|x-2|}{x-2}\to-1$ as $x\to2^-$ and $\to1$ as $x\to2^+$. Thus the pair is $(3,5)$.

Independent check: For x<2, |x−2|=−(x−2), so f(x)=x+1 and the left limit is 3. For x>2, |x−2|=x−2, so f(x)=x+3 and the right limit is 5.
solution:
For $x<2$, $|x-2|=-(x-2)$, so $f(x)=x+1$ and $\lim_{x\to2^-}f(x)=3$.
For $x>2$, $|x-2|=x-2$, so $f(x)=x+3$ and $\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)=5$.
Thus the pair is $(3,5)$.
